tasks.title: Migrate the frontmatter role maps
tasks.acceptance: engine.RoleOverride carries Focus []string alongside Enabled *bool. Frontmatter.ReviewRoles alongside Frontmatter.AuditRoles become map[string]RoleOverride with parseRoleOverrides writing the struct. The three invalidated test files are updated in the same commit so the gate stays green: frontmatter_roleoverrides_test.go, overrides_test.go, lens_shim_test.go.
source_sections: ### 2.2 The parsed override becomes a struct
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.RoleOverride added in internal/engine/frontmatter.go carrying Focus []string alongside Enabled *bool (nil = unset = pre-v0.32.0 behavior); verified by go build ./... exit 0 and by the engine test package compiling and passing against the new type.
- Frontmatter.ReviewRoles and Frontmatter.AuditRoles are now map[string]RoleOverride, written by parseRoleOverrides on all three write paths (absent focus, focus: null, parsed list) and defaulted by defaultFrontmatter; the reading call sites moved with the type — ResolveOverrideFocus (overrides.go) reads overrides[id].Focus and TranslateLegacyLens (lens_shim.go) returns map[string]RoleOverride leaving Enabled nil since the legacy lens cannot deactivate a role. Verified by TestParseFrontmatter_RoleOverrides / _RoleOverrideDisallowedKey / _RoleOverrideShapeWarnings / _NoRoleOverrides and TestResolveOverrideFocus_* / TestTranslateLegacyLens_* all passing with unchanged behavior (enabled is not parsed yet; the '(only focus)' warning literal is still asserted verbatim).
- Invalidated tests updated in this same commit 49eff04: frontmatter_roleoverrides_test.go (5 assertions) and lens_shim_test.go (6 assertions) now read .Focus; overrides_test.go builds no override map literals and calls ResolveOverrideFocus through its unchanged two-value signature, so it compiled and passed untouched — the third return value it will need arrives with the §2.3 task. domain_lens_test.go left alone per §6.1. Gate verified with separate exit codes before closing: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0 (0 issues); dogfooded with a freshly built /tmp/tp-dev/tp (tp lint spec/0.32.0.md exit 0).

tasks.title: Permit enabled in override objects
tasks.acceptance: The permitted override key set gains enabled so it no longer warns. The unpermitted-key warning text becomes (only focus and enabled) with every existing literal assertion updated. Test 5 passes.

- Out of scope: parsing the boolean into RoleOverride.Enabled remains nil-only, per the task fence (the next task).

tasks.title: Parse a boolean enabled value
tasks.acceptance: A boolean enabled populates RoleOverride.Enabled. An enabled of true is accepted as a no-op leaving the role active with its focus layered. Test 3 passes.

tasks.title: Treat a null enabled as unset
tasks.acceptance: An explicit enabled of null decodes to nil with no warning. A valueless enabled key behaves identically. Test 14 passes.

tasks.title: Return the enabled-false drop set
tasks.acceptance: ResolveOverrideFocus returns a third value carrying the ids dropped for a false enabled. Both callers under internal/cli receive it. The existing overrides tests assert the third value.
source_sections: ### 2.3 Resolution drops the role and reports what it dropped

tasks.title: Apply the drop outside ResolveActiveCorpus
tasks.acceptance: The drop is applied after ResolveActiveCorpus domain filtering rather than inside it. A spec deactivating every user role never falls back to the embedded corpus. Test 11 passes.
source_sections: ### 2.3 Resolution drops the role and reports what it dropped

tasks.title: Warn when no active role matches
tasks.acceptance: A false enabled on an id in no corpus warns matches no active role while changing nothing. A role removed by domains takes the same path appearing once in skipped_roles with domain-mismatch. Tests 6 alongside 13 pass.
source_sections: ### 2.3 Resolution drops the role and reports what it dropped

tasks.title: Report deactivated roles as disabled-by-spec
tasks.acceptance: Every role deactivated by a false enabled is named in skipped_roles with the reason disabled-by-spec. This holds for the review payload as well as the audit payload. Test 1 passes.

tasks.title: Drop focus from a deactivated role
tasks.acceptance: A false enabled with focus on the same role deactivates that role. Its focus is applied nowhere in the output. Test 2 passes.

tasks.title: Keep skipped_roles omitted under compact
tasks.acceptance: The compact flag omits skipped_roles including disabled-by-spec entries. Test 16 passes.

tasks.title: Suppress the lens shim on deactivation
tasks.acceptance: A spec whose only review_roles entry is a false enabled suppresses the legacy lens shim. Test 12 passes.
source_sections: ### 2.3 Resolution drops the role and reports what it dropped

tasks.title: Refuse a phase with no roles
tasks.acceptance: Emitting prompts for a phase whose active roles are all dropped exits 2. The message renders as every <phase> role is deactivated by this spec followed by the ids, with the phase word taken from PhaseReviewers or PhaseAuditors. The hint reads re-enable at least one role, or remove the enabled: false entries.

tasks.title: List only spec-deactivated ids
tasks.acceptance: The empty-phase id list carries only the ids this spec deactivated, sorted comma-separated. Ids already absent through domains or a missing role file are excluded. A phase emptied partly by domains names only the deactivated ones.

tasks.title: Exclude regression from the emptiness check
tasks.acceptance: The built-in regression role does not count as an active reviewer for the emptiness check. A review spec deactivating every corpus reviewer still exits 2. Test 9 passes.

tasks.title: Resolve roles ahead of every write
tasks.acceptance: Corpus resolution alongside override resolution run ahead of EnsureReviewState in tp review. They run ahead of the snapshot write in tp audit. Test 7 asserts a refused run writes no state directory, no state file, no round snapshot.

tasks.title: Refuse deactivating the spec-coverage auditor
tasks.acceptance: An auditor drop set containing spec-coverage exits 2 with the message spec-coverage cannot be deactivated: it carries the entire spec-derived checklist. The hint reads remove the enabled: false entry for spec-coverage. It fires even when other auditors remain active.

tasks.title: Key the refusal on the drop set
tasks.acceptance: The refusal keys on the drop set rather than on the frontmatter entry. Identical frontmatter exits 2 against an auditor corpus holding the spec-coverage role file but warns matches no active role against a populated corpus lacking it. A review_roles entry naming spec-coverage always takes the warning path.

tasks.title: Report spec-coverage before empty phase
tasks.acceptance: The checks are decided in the order given by the precedence section. A spec tripping both refusals reports the spec-coverage one. Test 10 passes.

tasks.title: Fire refusals only on prompt emission
tasks.acceptance: Neither refusal fires under the review record, status, merge, resolve, resolve-all, verify or report modes. Neither fires under the audit record, status or merge modes. Test 8 asserts the absence of the two literal messages rather than a non-2 exit code.

tasks.title: Assert perspective bypasses corpus resolution
tasks.acceptance: The review perspective mode short-circuits before the corpus is resolved. It emits its single fixed prompt carrying neither refusal message. The perspective half of test 8 passes.

tasks.title: Keep roles_hash free of frontmatter overrides
tasks.acceptance: Toggling enabled changes the recorded round spec_hash. It leaves roles_hash unchanged, proving the override is not fed into ComputeRolesHash. Test 15 passes with the roles_hash clause as the discriminating assertion.

tasks.title: Document the lever in four files
tasks.acceptance: README.md, skills/tp/SKILL.md, skills/tp/REFERENCE.md alongside the role-corpus rule in CLAUDE.md each contain the substring enabled: false deactivates a role for one spec. Each states the disabled-by-spec reason alongside the two emission-only refusals. Each states that domains is the durable axis while a false enabled is the one-spec exception.

tasks.title: State both trim-candidate levers in REFERENCE
tasks.acceptance: REFERENCE.md states that a trim candidate has two levers guarded differently. It states that deleting the role file is unguarded, including for spec-coverage, removing nothing when it is the phase last role file. It states that tp does not guard against deactivating a role with open findings.

tasks.title: Guard the four documents with a test
tasks.acceptance: A guard test asserts the four documents contain the pinned substring. It asserts REFERENCE.md states both trim-candidate levers. Test 17 passes.
